sources.title: Lenny Product Strategy: Finding a wedge
sources.author: Lenny Rachitsky

chunks.text: The best founders start by discovering the narrowest valuable problem instead of chasing a broad market. A wedge is a clear customer pain that creates urgency and makes a product feel necessary.
When teams focus on one segment and one recurring job, the feedback loop becomes sharper. They can learn whether people keep returning and whether the product meaningfully changes behavior.
Strong product growth tends to come from repeated learning, not from launching an overbuilt platform with no signal from users.
A good experiment is the smallest test that answers a business question. The goal is not to build a complicated dashboard but to learn whether the customer relationship is worth doubling down on.
Retention, referral language, and real usage are much more informative than vanity metrics. You want evidence that people are changing behavior because your product creates value.
A practical growth plan begins by isolating the single behavior you want to change and then measuring whether the intervention moves it in the right direction.
